opportunities.name: Improving HPV uptake in school leavers living in areas of high deprivation
opportunities.authority: NHS England
opportunities.description:
The HPV vaccine remains one of the most effective vaccines, providing long-lasting protection against several strains of the human papillomavirus that is known to cause cervical, vaginal, vulval, anal, penile, and head/neck cancers. A single dose of the vaccine is offered to boys and girls aged 12-13 years old through the School Aged Immunisation Service (SAIS).
With the COVID-19 pandemic causing significant disruptions to delivery, resulting in a reduction in overall coverage, uptake rates have failed to recover to pre-pandemic levels.
There is increasing evidence that HPV uptake is lower among socio-economically deprived groups, with lower coverage associated with lower IMD among older adolescents in the initial catch-up programme that was delivered in schools and other settings between 2008-2011.
Catch-up campaigns, including the GP HPV campaign, provide individuals who missed the routine offer with an additional opportunity to be vaccinated. Capturing learning from these campaigns and associated activities is essential to identify effective approaches, inform future delivery models, and determine what further action may be required to reduce inequalities in uptake.

opportunities.description: NHS England is seeking to appoint a supplier to deliver the Step into Health programme, a national workforce support service designed to support members of the Armed Forces community, including service leavers, veterans and their family members, into employment within the NHS. The programme will provide a comprehensive range of services including employer engagement, candidate support, recruitment pathways, career guidance, mentoring, work placements, communications and outreach activities, stakeholder engagement, and the operation of a dedicated candidate management system. The service will work collaboratively with NHS organisations, the Ministry of Defence, the Career Transition Partnership, military charities and other key stakeholders to promote NHS career opportunities, reduce barriers to employment, widen participation, and support Armed Forces community members in securing sustainable careers within the NHS. opportunities.authority: Birmingham Women's and Children's NHS Foundation Trust
opportunities.description:
Specialist Inpatient Peer Support Worker Programme

NHSE recognises peer support as a supported self-management intervention. It happens when people with similar long-term conditions, or health experiences, come together to support each other – either on a one-to-one or group basis. It is enabled through relationships that build mutual acceptance and understanding. Peer support is a valuable resource for people and their families and carers; empowering them to take ownership of, and have more control over, their health and wellbeing. It enables people to develop the knowledge, skills and confidence to self-manage and address other issues that might be affecting their health, such as loneliness or self-esteem. The power of peer support lies in connecting people with shared experience to create an encouraging, inspiring, and safe space. This personalised, holistic support focuses on wellbeing and understanding lived experience, rather than clinical interventions.

The Child Sexual Assault Assessment Services in North and West Yorkshire are specialist, trauma‑informed services providing holistic care for children and young people who may have experienced sexual assault or abuse. The service delivers timely forensic medical assessment and evidence collection, alongside treatment of injuries and sexual health care, within a safe, child‑friendly environment. It operates through multi‑agency pathways with police, children’s social care and safeguarding partners, ensuring robust protection and coordinated response. opportunities.name: Provision of broadband Connectivity Services for SD‑WAN Deployment
opportunities.authority: Torbay and South Devon NHS Foundation Trust
opportunities.description:
The Devon Procurement Service are undertaking this procurement on behalf of Torbay and South Devon NHS Foundation Trust. The DPS is made up 5 NHS entities (University Hospital Plymouth NHS Trust, Torbay & South Devon Foundation Trust, Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust , Devon Partnership Trust, Livewell Southwest). Torbay operates many community sites that are currently connected using BT LES circuits. These services are expensive, inflexible and no longer fit with how we want to operate our network. 

We are in the process of rolling out SD‑WAN with centrally managed firewalls. This is a key part of our cyber security strategy and will allow us to properly segment and segregate community sites from the wider Trust network. It will also improve resilience while reducing ongoing connectivity costs. 

To make this work, we need modern, reliable and resilient broadband connectivity at every community site. Each site must have two independent connections so that loss of a single circuit, route or supplier does not take the site offline.

opportunities.name: Complex Termination of Pregnancy (CTOP) Services across the South East (Mkt Eng)
opportunities.authority: NHS South, Central and West Commissioning Support Unit (hosted by NHS England)
opportunities.description:
The Commissioner is seeking suitable providers who have the capability and capacity to deliver Complex Termination of Pregnancy (CTOP) service, in line with the specified requirements, in the capacity of the Regional Network Lead Provider (Hub) responsible for the delivery, coordination and clinical governance of CTOP pathways across the South East region

The procurement will establish one Regional Lead Centre (Hub) responsible for:
•	Hosting the Single Point of Access (SPOA) for all CTOP referrals in the South East.
•	Leading the Regional Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) to review, triage, and allocate cases across the network.
•	Delivering direct clinical care for patients requiring both medical and surgical terminations up to 23 + 6 weeks’ gestation.
•	Providing clinical governance and quality oversight for all Network Member Providers (Spokes).
•	Leading the training, upskilling, and maintenance-of-skills programme for the regional CTOP workforce, in line with the national CTOP service specification.
•	Coordinating regional data collection, audit, outcome reporting, and shared learning to ensure consistent standards of care across the South East.

opportunities.authority: East of England Collaborative Procurement Hub
opportunities.description:
This is the first re-opening of the Social Impact Framework.

The EoECPH Social Impact Framework aims to provide a structured, compliant procurement route for services that deliver social betterment and impact, aligning with NHS and government priorities such as reducing inequalities, improving community well-being, and enhancing sustainability.
This Framework will support NHS trusts and Integrated Care Boards (ICBs) in procuring high-quality services that address key social challenges, including homelessness, financial inclusion, employment support, offender rehabilitation, and community integration.

While Voluntary, Community, and Social Enterprises (VCSEs) and SMEs currently deliver many of these services, the Framework will be open to all eligible suppliers, ensuring full compliance with the Procurement Act 2023.
The Framework will:
•	Simplify access to suppliers delivering social impact services.
•	Ensure compliance under the Procurement Act 2023.
•	Improve efficiency by providing a pre-qualified list of suppliers.
•	Drive social and economic development.

opportunities.name: NHSE1116 - RFI - Accredited Pulmonary Rehabilitation Programme Support Service
opportunities.authority: NHS North of England Commissioning Support Unit (hosted by NHS England)
opportunities.description:
The Commissioners require a Accredited Pulmonary Rehabilitation Programme Support Service to assist the Healthcare and Gymnasium teams within the Adult Prisons in North East & Yorkshire in delivering an ongoing programme of Accredited Pulmonary Rehabilitation for the patients in their care.  It is hoped that outcomes would include improved health and well-being for patients and a reduction in exacerbation's, which in turn would reduce the numbers of patients requiring access to secondary and/or specialised services. 

The Accredited Pulmonary Rehabilitation Programme Support Service will develop virtual training packages for use with patients within Prisons, provide training for staff and provide a ‘critical friend’ / QA service for Prison Healthcare and Gymnasium staff to enable them to support the patients within their care. It is also expected that should there be any changes to national guidance on the delivery of Pulmonary Rehabilitation, the virtual training packages and staff training will be updated and disseminated.  The contract will be for 2-years in the first instance and an independent review will also be Commissioned to ascertain the value for money and effectivenes

opportunities.name: Frailty Consultant Services across Brent and Harrow

opportunities.description:
An integrated medical model for CLCH’s Rapid Response, Care Home Teams & Falls Services across the boroughs of Brent and Harrow. This model will enhance operational efficiency and improve patient safety and quality of care in the frailty and falls services across Brent and Harrow. 
The primary purpose of the Frailty Service is to be clinically accountable for the Integrated Rapid Response, Enhanced Care Home Team (ECHT), Integrated Case Management (ICM), and Falls Services across Brent and Harrow, while providing clinical leadership and support to the Rapid Response team. The consultant(s) will be responsible for delivering high-quality medical care, preventing hospital admissions, and managing complex cases in the community. This role requires taking full accountability for clinical outcomes, ensuring that the consultant(s) leads the service with clear responsibility for decision-making and patient care. The consultant(s) will work closely with multidisciplinary teams to ensure seamless service integration and optimal patient outcomes.

The scope of this RFI is limited to exploring provider capability, capacity, digital maturity and interoperability required to support the electronic ordering of diagnostic tests, appointment booking, and digital return of results across England.
This market engagement is pre procurement in nature and is intended to inform the development of NHS Online’s future commercial and sourcing strategy for diagnostic access. It does not seek to commission diagnostic services, determine commercial or contractual models, or identify suppliers for any future procurement. Responses will be used solely to improve NHS Online’s understanding of the current market and potential delivery models that could support digitally enabled diagnostic access at scale.

This project will provide 1:1 English language, linguistic, and communication skills support for Resident Doctors referred through the Midlands Professional Support and Wellbeing (PSW) service. The support is designed for trainees whose first language is not English and aims to strengthen clinical communication, interpersonal effectiveness, confidence, and cultural and linguistic awareness.
The appointed provider(s) will be expected to:
•Enhance residents’ spoken English, including fluency, clarity, and confidence.
• Support residents to develop socially appropriate, patient-centred communication skills relevant to clinical practice.
• Address specific linguistic or cultural barriers that may be affecting exam performance, workplace integration, or clinical interactions.
• Deliver structured assessments, personalised learning plans, and measurable progress updates to evidence improvement.

opportunities.name: Theatres Managed Service - RFI
opportunities.authority: Gloucestershire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
opportunities.description:
Gloucestershire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (GHFT) is embarking on the re-procurement of its Theatres Managed Equipment Service (MES). The Trust currently operates a Theatres MES valued at approximately £25m per year, including equipment provision, theatre related consumables, sterile services, refurbishment, engineering support, specialist cleaning, waste management, and facilities maintenance across both Gloucestershire Royal Hospital and Cheltenham General Hospital.
The current contract is approaching the end of its full term, and the Trust are looking to explore the re-procurement of the Theatres MES. As the development of the future service model and commercial strategy progresses, we are seeking valuable insight and expertise from suppliers with the capability to deliver a comprehensive Theatres MES, required to operate the surgical facilities across both sites, in addition to potential wider expansion across adjacent areas including interventional radiology, cardiology, endoscopy, and other areas. 
As part of this early market engagement exercise, GHFT invites interested suppliers to feedback on our future model.

opportunities.description: The scope of this tender is to procure an automated pharmacy storage and fulfilment solution capable of managing approximately 3,000+ pharmaceutical products across chilled (+2°C to +8°C) and ambient (+15°C to +24°C) environments, with future flexibility for ultra‑low‑temperature storage. opportunities.name: Strategic Commissioning Framework – Development Programme

opportunities.description:
Delivering the NHS 10-Year Plan depends fundamentally on restoring and strengthening commissioning. It will require commissioners with the capability, authority and confidence to reshape services, challenge existing models of provision and use every lever to drive change

ICBs are now stewards of over £130 billion of NHS funding, with an average system responsible for around £5 billion each year. This unprecedented scale, coupled with the new multi-year planning and financial framework, provides a renewed opportunity to manage risk differently; to pool resources, shift investment upstream, and reshape local markets. 

NHS England want to establish a national Strategic Commissioning Development Programme (SCDP) for 2026/27–2027/28 and this notice is to highlight a potential forthcoming procurement for a consortium of partners to assist the design and delivery of the action learning programme as a key part of the wider Strategic Commissioning Development Programme. opportunities.name: Early Market Engagement on Health and Work Outcomes‑Based Contracting
opportunities.authority: Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC)
opportunities.description:
Description:

The Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC), working with NHS England, is undertaking an early market engagement to inform the potential development of Health and Growth outcomes‑based contracts. These contracts would aim to support people with health conditions to remain in, or return to, sustained employment, contributing to wider objectives around economic growth and reducing health‑related economic inactivity.

Levels of economic inactivity driven by long-term health conditions continue to rise. Around 2.8 million people in the UK are currently out of work for health reasons, up from 2 million in 2019. A further 4.1 million people remain in work, but live with one or more work-limiting conditions, an increase from 300,000 people over the past year.

This early market engagement aims to help DHSC-NHSE understand how investors and providers could work with government to address health-related economic inactivity, and to ensure that the proposed outcomes-based contracts are attractive, deliverable, and mutually beneficial for ahead of any formal market launch. opportunities.name: 4-year Fellowship - endpoint toxicity for a mixture of chemicals
opportunities.authority: Food Standards Agency
opportunities.description:
Without OPSS £670k, with OPSS £620k (TBC whether OPSS will be involved). 
This four‑year Fellowship will develop and evaluate a tiered in silico and in vitro New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) framework to predict human‑relevant toxicity from mixtures of chemicals, using a food-relevant group of chemicas such as phthalates or PFASs as a case study. Building on the successes of the 2020 FSA Computational Toxicology Fellowship and recent international resgurgence in interest in mixtures assessment, the project will aim to generate new data, models, and tools to improve the understanding of complex chemical interactions and to support regulatory decision‑making. The Fellowship will also explore data ecosystems across UK government (potentially with OPSS), strengthening capability in data storage, curation, and interrogation, while contributing a high‑quality UK case study that continues to develop confidence in NAMs for chemical risk assessment.

opportunities.authority: NHS Coventry and Warwickshire Integrated Care Board
opportunities.description:
The Ophthalmology Coordination Service Hub (OCS) will support the system-wide approach to the management for all non-emergency (routine and urgent) ophthalmology referrals from community Optometry practices across Coventry and Warwickshire ICB and Hereford and Worcester ICB. The OCS will provide a single point of access, administering all incoming referrals from community Optometrists, offering patients a choice of providers in accordance with patient choice regulations, and submitting onward referrals to secondary care (accredited independent sector or NHS provision).

The OCS supports the streamlining of ophthalmology referrals across the ICS, reducing delays to patients being referred from the community to secondary care and freeing up primary care capacity. For every routine and urgent referral, the service will provide patients with choice of access based on the referring condition, supporting patients being seen by the right person, in the right place, the first time.

The service will not undertake clinical triage of incoming referrals.

This service will be Procured as 2 separate lots covering both ICB's.

opportunities.name: Market Engagement for Transdermal Capillary Blood Sampling Solutions
opportunities.authority: Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC)
opportunities.description:
Background:

The 10 Year Health Plan for England (10YHP) sets out a clear ambition to shift care from hospitals into neighbourhood and community settings. Diagnostics are a critical enabler of this shift, ensuring that people can monitor long‑term conditions, receive preventative testing, or be rapidly triaged without needing to attend acute sites. Remote and community‑based blood sampling therefore represents a significant opportunity to improve patient access, support earlier diagnosis, and reduce pressures on primary and secondary care services.

This market engagement exercise aims to understand the range of venous‑equivalent transdermal capillary blood sampling devices currently available, and to explore opportunities to pilot their use in community pharmacy settings and potentially in people’s homes. This is particularly important for groups who face barriers to accessing traditional phlebotomy services, including people with learning disabilities, those with needle phobia, homeless populations, and other underserved communities.

opportunities.name: RFI - Temperature Monitoring System
opportunities.authority: North London NHS Foundation Trust
opportunities.description:
This specification outlines the requirements for implementing a modern, wireless medical temperature monitoring system across the North East London NHS Foundation Trust (NELFT). The primary objective of this system is to ensure the safe and secure storage of medicines and clinical supplies, which must be maintained within strict temperature ranges to preserve efficacy and comply with regulatory standards.
The proposed solution will replace the existing temperature monitoring infrastructure, which has not been upgraded or maintained since its initial deployment. The new system must deliver accurate, real-time temperature data for all medical refrigerators and designated drug storage areas, providing 24/7 remote monitoring and full data visibility. This will enable proactive management, reduce compliance risks, and support adherence to national and local governance requirements.

opportunities.name: Evaluation of NHSE Education Quality Data Indicators
opportunities.authority: NHS England
opportunities.description: The National Education and Training Survey (NETS) launched in 2019 and has since provided the only national platform to collect feedback from learners and professionals working across the full breadth of the health and care system. This insight into learner experience is vital in reducing student attrition, improving workforce retention and reducing inequalities and discrimination. The NETS questions have evolved over time and additional features, such as professional branching, have been added. After six years it is important that the current question set is independently validated for content and dependability along with the statistical model used to analyse the response dataset. opportunities.name: Cognitive Stimulation Therapy Service for people with mild to moderate Dementia
opportunities.authority: NHS Hampshire and Isle of Wight Integrated Care Board
opportunities.description:
The Cognitive Stimulation Therapy (CST) service provides structured, evidence-based group therapy to support people living with mild to moderate stages of a dementia. The program consists of themed activities designed to actively stimulate and engage individuals, while promoting social interaction and cognitive function. It is currently the only non-drug treatment recommended by the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) for mild to moderate dementia. 
The aims of the service are: 
•	Maintain or improve cognitive functioning and quality of life.
•	Enhance communication and social interaction.
•	Delay the inevitable progression of dementia
•	Support individuals to remain active, engaged, and independent for as long as possible

opportunities.name: Adult Community Services Market Engagement Event
opportunities.authority: NHS Surrey Heartlands Integrated Care Board
opportunities.description:
NHS Surrey Heartlands Integrated Care Board (SHICB) invites providers to join our first Market Engagement event as we begin shaping the future of Out-of-Hospital services. This event marks the start of a collaborative journey to shape models that deliver on the NHS 10 Year Health Plan and achieve the three strategic shifts, moving care from hospital to community, transforming from analogue to digital, and shifting the focus from sickness to prevention.

Please join us on 5th December 2025 when Jack Wagstaff, Executive Director of Strategic Commissioning, will relay early service scoping considerations and the questions we are asking ourselves regarding the most appropriate configurations and models for Surrey citizens. We hope to hear provider insights, innovative ideas, and preferences to inform the scope of a forthcoming procurement programme.

opportunities.description:
The Department of Health and Social Care seeks to commission an external partner to deliver a regional pilot of the Waiting Well service for eligible for individuals aged 18+ who on the current waiting list for adult gender services based in the southwest of England and awaiting their first appointment. 

The service’s primary focus is to provide a holistic approach that integrates wellbeing support, with the aim of achieving the following outcomes: 

Improved self-reported wellbeing and resilience  

Increased readiness for first appointment with gender dysphoria clinic  

Increased ability to self-manage symptoms while awaiting clinical care.  

Reduced isolation and increased social connectedness.  

Reduced unplanned use of crisis or emergency services.

opportunities.description:
NHSE intends to engage with suppliers to facilitate their listing via the Digital Buyer's Catalogue. An Engagement Approach has been identified to ensure that suitably qualified suppliers and systems are taken forward for assurance. 

The process will be undertaken in three stages:

Qualification - validates the company information of the Respondent to ensure suitability to become a supplier of services supporting public health operations, 

System Readiness Gateway - managing Respondent's timing through the development and assurance assessment process in line with the readiness of their system against the published NHSE Capabilities and Standards; and,

Assurance Process - qualifying the Respondent's system to provide the Services through evaluation against nationally published standards 

This notice begins the process via the Qualification Process described above. Suppliers will be required to complete a Pre-Qualification Questionnaire, which will be evaluated to ensure that their company is suitable and that they have a solution which can be taken forward for assurance in stages 2 and 3.

opportunities.name: Strategic Commissioning Framework – Development Programme
opportunities.authority: NHS England
opportunities.description:
NHS are undertaking a Request for Information (RFI) exercise using the SBS Framework (Consultancy and Advisory Services for Health), and wish to engage with suppliers listed on Lot 2: Integrated care, healthcare and community care to understand the opportunities to deliver, with external support, a structured programme of support for leaders and middle managers within ICBs (the “Development Programme”).
NHS England are preparing to publish the NHS Strategic Commissioning Framework shortly which will set out the core enablers and activities associated with the four pillars of commissioning. 
Following publication, we will be co-designing with ICBs and other commissioning entities a range of support to help them build the skills, knowledge, behaviours.
The programme will be jointly delivered with NHS England and should consider the opportunities for a blended team approach, working jointly with NHS England national and regional teams and ICB colleagues to maximise the opportunities for successful delivery, shared learning and knowledge transfer.

opportunities.authority: NHS South East London Integrated Care Board
opportunities.description:
Southwark Council and NHS South East London ICB are seeking a lead provider to deliver the Southwark Wellbeing Hub, a borough-wide mental health and wellbeing support service. 
The Southwark Wellbeing Hub is a key part of Southwark’s integrated care system, offering accessible, culturally competent, and community-led support to adult residents experiencing low to moderate mental health needs.

The recommissioned service will operate across a physical hub in the Southwark Resource Centre, multiple satellite ‘spoke sites’, and outreach settings. 

The service will deliver six core work packages:
1.	Information, Advice and Guidance (IAG)
2.	Group Work
3.	Peer Support
4.	One-to-One Support (including specialist roles)
5.	Front Door to Adult Social Care
6.	Bespoke Counselling Intervention for Global Majority Communities

Key features:
•	Hub-and-spoke model based at Southwark Resource Centre with satellite delivery across five neighbourhoods.
•	Multidisciplinary workforce including specialist keyworkers and counsellors.
•	Subcontracting encouraged to grassroots and community organisations.
•	Ringfenced funding of £100,000–£120,000 per annum for culturally competent couns

opportunities.description:
NHS England is inviting bids from experienced suppliers to deliver the One NHS Finance (ONF) programme, a strategic initiative aimed at strengthening the NHS finance function across England. 
The ONF programme is designed to:
•	Improve staff retention, career progression, and workforce diversity.
•	Build capacity and capacity within NHS finance departments.
•	Promote excellence and innovation in finance management across the English NHS.
The overarching goal of ONF is to ensure that all NHS finance staff have equitable access to the opportunities they need to grow their skills, thrive in their roles, and progress their careers. 
The successful supplier will host the ONF service, working in close collaboration with the Finance Leadership Council and a broad network of national and regional steering groups.
The selected supplier is expected to commence work in early January 2026.
Contract Details:

opportunities.description:
The Radiology Service at Gloucestershire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (GHFT) provides a comprehensive range of diagnostic and interventional imaging procedures. A core element of this service is the delivery of accurate and timely diagnostic reports for acute and elective patients, which is essential to enable precise diagnosis and effective treatment planning across a wide spectrum of medical conditions.

Since May 2015, GHFT has utilised external reporting provision to supplement in-house capacity and ensure reporting times are maintained within nationally recognised standards. This outsourcing support has been critical in reducing delays in patient care, improving efficiency within elective reporting, and supporting the Authority in managing sustained increases in demand in a safe and sustainable way.

The following services, modalities, and sub-specialty reporting areas are included within the scope of this contract:
• Modalities. The current range of image reporting required under this specification includes, but is not limited to:
- Plain Radiography (Computed Radiography (CR)/ Digital Radiography (DR))
- Computed Tomography (CT)
- Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI)

By establishing a better “fingerprint” of STEC strains typically associated with livestock farm types, we can attribute the proportion of human STEC cases to different livestock species which will help to understand sources and pathways of contamination of secondary food types such as salad crops.  Understanding what proportion of human cases of STEC are attributable to different livestock farm types may also help growers take a proportionate risk management approach to protecting consumers.

opportunities.name: PRJ 2198 – NEL  Community Vasectomy Services
opportunities.authority: NHS North East London Integrated Care Board
opportunities.description:
The service  relates to the provision of a high quality, safe, community consultant-led no-scalpel vasectomy service comprising of pre-operative counselling, procedure and post vasectomy testing.

The service aims to provide a quality and safe non-scalpel technique vasectomy procedure under Local Anaesthetic (LA) in a primary care setting accordance with the Faculty of Sexual and Reproductive Healthcare (FSRH),guidelines (April 2024) for all residents living within North East London boroughs. This will be in a community care setting from various local sites ensuring that is easily accessible to all residents of the North East London geography.

Other objectives are:
•	To provide a service that complies with accepted best practice in line with national and local guidance, relevant accreditations processes, relevant guidelines in clinical practices and robust governance arrangements.
•	To provide a complete holistic patient focussed care package which includes pre- and post-operative care information, advice and counselling
•	To provide an opportunity for the promotion of men’s health
•	To provide a cost-effective service

The offer will be made available for young people aged up to 25 where there are additional vulnerabilities indicating they would likely benefit from a youth work (rather than adult support service) approach. 

Young people who access support from this offer are likely to be experiencing social, emotional, and mental health and wellbeing challenges and the provider will be experienced in providing support and promoting recovery for young people with these needs.

opportunities.name: High geochemical lead survey
opportunities.authority: Food Standards Agency
opportunities.description:
Sampling for lead in food produced or grown in high geochemical lead areas of the GB.

The levels of lead present in food can vary depending on several factors, one being the presence of (high) levels of geochemical lead in the location in which food products have or are being grown or reared.

There are maximum levels for lead in some foods and due to the variable nature of the presence of geochemical lead throughout the UK, it is necessary that the FSA has an understanding on the levels of lead in food products grown or reared in medium/high geochemical lead (ranges TBD from literature data).

The work is considered one of the FSA’s main areas of research interest (under chemical hazards; including nanomaterials and microplastics) and will be used to inform long-term policy and/or strategic decision making.

opportunities.description:
The Carers’ Support Service in North East Lincolnshire (NEL) is designed to promote, support and improve the mental, physical and emotional wellbeing of all carers. Its aim is to ensure carers can continue in their caring role where this is their choice, while also maintaining their own health, independence and life opportunities such as work, training, education, leisure and social interaction.

The service will be person-centred, culturally sensitive and inclusive, with carers actively involved in shaping decisions and influencing delivery. It will proactively identify carers of all ages, including hidden carers, and provide accessible support through a central hub in Grimsby and a network of local spokes in community venues. Carers will be encouraged to register with the service, with a target of at least 800 new registrations each year, and will be able to access advice, information, signposting and referrals, including to carers’ needs assessments where appropriate.

The main objective of the FSA’s strategy for 2022-2027 is to ensure that food is safe, is what it says that it is and that it is healthier and more sustainable. With this, our role is to protect consumers from unacceptable risks linked to the consumption of food. Under the regulated products research programme, this includes producing evidence to support thorough, well informed, risk assessments for novel ingredients proposed for the UK market.
Cell cultivated products (CCPs) and alternative proteins produced by biomass or precision fermentation are an emergent food sector around the world. The FSA CCP Sandbox programme is a two-year programme designed to inform regulatory actions that strike the right balance between supporting innovation and ensuring consumers safety. CCPs products claim to have benefits in protein quality, environmental impact, and improved animal welfare implications. Short-term community beds are a core component of the intermediate care offer in Leeds, supporting people for a short period in a community bed when they are unable to be supported in their usual place of residence and do not require hospital care.

opportunities.name: Birmingham Children's Hospital Water Tank Replacement
opportunities.authority: Birmingham Women's and Children's NHS Foundation Trust
opportunities.description: The works comprise the upgrade of the Trust’s water storage on site. The Work is located in the existing Towers of Block P (East and West Towers). The scheme involves the provision of new storage tanks and associated new pipework/systems connecting onto the existing infrastructure systems being retained. The works will involve a contractor design solution to provide the new mezzanine floors to support the new storage tanks including altering and adapting the means of access to the new/existing facility. Whilst the majority of the new installation works can be undertaken simultaneously, the final connections/bringing the new tanks/system live must be done sequentially. The contractor will be required to commission (including chlorination) the first tank to allow partial possession of the works prior to commencing the final connection works for the second tank. It is envisaged that the existing tanks will still be in use to allow draw off of water from the existing tanks until empty and the new tanks are fully commissioned. The contractor is required as part of their submission to provide a cost for emptying the tanks and removing the same.

opportunities.name: C385933 Works to Linen Store and Bed Store
opportunities.authority: 2Gether Support Solutions Limited
opportunities.description:
2gether Support Solutions is seeking a suitably experienced contractor (the ‘Supplier’) to carry out works to its existing Linen Store and Bed Store at the William Harvey Hospital in Ashford. 

Following a space change of use within the hospital some rooms have become available which we would like to refurbish and change the use of.  
We have an area which was used for storage of linen before it was decanted around the hospital, which we would like to convert into an office environment creating 3 closed offices and one large open plan office.  
We have another area which we would like to use to create a welcoming welfare environment for staff. Currently staff do not have any are in which to take a break therefore this would provide them with a much needed wellbeing area.  
The indicative start date for the works is 24/10/2025 and we would expect the works to take 6-8 weeks to complete. 
The works will need to be phased. Phase 1 will convert the existing linen store into an office and change the single door on the corridor to a double door set.  The second phase will include the refurbishment of the old bed store into a welfare facility.

opportunities.authority: NHS Hampshire and Isle of Wight Integrated Care Board
opportunities.description:
The Cognitive Stimulation Therapy (CST) service provides structured, evidence-based group therapy to support people living with mild to moderate stages of a dementia. The program consists of themed activities designed to actively stimulate and engage individuals, while promoting social interaction and cognitive function. It is currently the only non-drug treatment recommended by the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) for mild to moderate dementia. 
The aims of the service are: 
•	Maintain or improve cognitive functioning and quality of life.
•	Enhance communication and social interaction.
•	Delay the inevitable progression of dementia
•	Support individuals to remain active, engaged, and independent for as long as possible

opportunities.name: Reducing declines in NBSS by boosting health professionals’ knowledge&confidence
opportunities.authority: NHS England
opportunities.description:
This project aims to:
• Identify any themes, trends, or patterns for parents who decline NBS screening for their babies. The highest decline rates have been amongst the ‘movers in’ population (‘movers in’ are babies who have either changed Integrated Care Board (ICB) or have moved in from another home nation or abroad). Babies who move into England are at risk of delayed or missed screening.
• Gain an insight into reasons why parents decline NBS and insight from health professionals offering the test.
• Improve the knowledge and confidence of health professionals offering and taking the sample to increase the uptake rates for targeted groups living in deprived areas identified by the data.
• Host a minimum of 6 training sessions delivered by experts either virtually, face to face or a combination of both.
• The production of a resource for use after the events, for reference and as an asset to keep the momentum going for new health professionals and a refresher for existing staff.

opportunities.name: Men's Health Partnership Opportunity
opportunities.authority: Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC)
opportunities.description:
Purpose of this Notice:
To support the publication of England’s inaugural men’s health strategy, the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) is interested in exploring collaboration opportunities with stakeholders from the voluntary, community, and social enterprise (VCSE) and private sectors to improve men’s health outcomes.
Men are disproportionately affected by conditions like heart disease, cancer, and type 2 diabetes—and 3 in 4 suicides in 2023 were men. Yet they're also less likely to seek support: for instance, men were 25% less likely than women to get a heart health check between 2012-2017. This is because men face many barriers to accessing, engaging, and having a positive experience with health and support services.
Following the ministerial roundtable hosted by DHSC on Wednesday, June 4th, 2025, DHSC is now seeking expressions of interest from organisations in the voluntary, community, and social enterprise (VCSE) and private sectors to collaborate in support of England’s first Men’s Health Strategy. opportunities.name: Medical Appraisals Service 2026-28
opportunities.authority: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
opportunities.description:
NICE’s is a designated body for medical revalidation for the medical practitioners it employs. NICE will support every doctor it employs, who wishes to continue to be licensed to practise, to achieve revalidation. To support revalidation NICE will help them to meet their professional commitments by facilitating an annual medical appraisal that complies with the professional standards set out by the GMC’s Good Medical Practice, the Royal Colleges and the Department of Health and Social Care.

NICE is the currently the designated body for 6 doctors. However, only those doctors that require a licence to practice for their role at NICE are included in the appraisal contract. This means that currently only 5 doctors with a prescribed connection to NICE need appraisals under this contract, as of 31 May 2025. It is therefore anticipated that a maximum of 8 doctors will need appraisals under this contract in any appraisal year. 

Current anticipated schedule of appraisals per year - January (1), February (1), April (1), August (1), August (1), December (1).

NICE is inviting applications from providers of medical appraisals to deliver the required number of appraisals for the doctors

opportunities.authority: Norfolk and Norwich University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
opportunities.description:
Norfolk and Waveney University Hospital Group (NWUHG) will be implementing a single Electronic Patient Record (EPR) across the three acute Trusts. This will enable increased integrated care both between the hospitals, and with the wider community. MEDITECH is the EPR solution that has been selected and there is an EPR programme in place to have this implemented by March 2026.

As part of the EPR Programme deliverables a Clinical Data Repository (CDR) solution that consolidates data from a variety of clinical sources to present a unified view of a single patient.
This solution is optimised to allow clinicians to retrieve data for a single patient rather than to identify a population of patients with common characteristics or to facilitate the management of a specific clinical department. 
The CDR will be also used as the archive solution which will retain data that is no longer actively used for long-term archiving and retention. Data that will be archived will  consists of older digital records and information that remains important to the organisation or must be retained for future reference or regulatory compliance reasons.

opportunities.name: Social Impact Framework (2025)
opportunities.authority: East of England Collaborative Procurement Hub
opportunities.description:
The EoECPH Social Impact Framework aims to provide a structured, compliant procurement route for services that deliver social betterment and impact, aligning with NHS and government priorities such as reducing inequalities, improving community well-being, and enhancing sustainability.
This Framework will support NHS trusts and Integrated Care Boards (ICBs) in procuring high-quality services that address key social challenges, including homelessness, financial inclusion, employment support, offender rehabilitation, and community integration.
While Voluntary, Community, and Social Enterprises (VCSEs) and SMEs currently deliver many of these services, the Framework will be open to all eligible suppliers, ensuring full compliance with the Procurement Act 2023.
The Framework will:
•	Simplify access to suppliers delivering social impact services.
•	Ensure compliance under the Procurement Act 2023.
•	Improve efficiency by providing a pre-qualified list of suppliers.
•	Drive social and economic development.

This procurement will be subject to the Light Touch Regime under the Procurement Act 2023

opportunities.name: Community Based Alternative Crisis Support Service
opportunities.authority: Central and North West London NHS Foundation Trust
opportunities.description:
Central North West London NHS Foundation Trust (CNWL) and West London NHS Trust (WLT) are seeking to commission an organisation who can co-produce six/eight community crisis alternative services, with our Experts by Experience (EBE) advisors, service users and carers, to be based in geographical locations across NW London boroughs.
The service will be a non-clinical service which will offer an open access safe space and calm environment for people who are experiencing mental health distress, in crisis, or need mental health advice. Without requiring an appointment, the provision will offer drop-in support, a warm drink, a listening ear, practical assistance, and the ability to refer or direct individuals to additional services if needed. The services will provide immediate practical support to reduce mental health distress and guide those with complex or urgent needs to the appropriate urgent care services. They help individuals manage their distress, develop healthy coping strategies, and ultimately aim to instil hope, self-worth, and purpose.

opportunities.name: DHSC: PCP: National HIV and STI Prevention Programme 2026
opportunities.authority: Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC)
opportunities.description:
THIS IS A PRELIMINARY MARKET ENGAGEMENT
The principal focus of the programme is the delivery of HIV and STI prevention interventions to key target groups, in whom the evidence demonstrates a higher or emerging burden of infection, at a national, regional and local level.
The programme is critical in ensuring that people are aware of how HIV and STIs are transmitted, how they can protect themselves, how and where to have an HIV and STI test and developments in HIV prevention and treatment.
Key objectives: 
A.	Improve awareness, knowledge, understanding and uptake of combination HIV and STI prevention interventions among populations most affected by HIV and STIs 
B.	Increase HIV and STI testing to reduce the undiagnosed population and proportion of late diagnoses
C.	Reduce levels of HIV related stigma, including within different communities, self-stigma and structural or institutional stigma 
D.	Enhance collaboration across national, regional and local partners and multi-sector organisations.

Engagement Event Date(s): 03/06/2025 

Background: The government has committed to end new HIV transmissions in England by 2030 and is developing a new HIV Action Plan (HIVAP) which will be published this year  

Collaboration is at the core of the new HIVAP, and the government is engaging with a wide range of system partners in its development, including people with lived experience, the voluntary and community sector, professional bodies, primary care, and local partners, amongst others. 

The new HIVAP will have 5 key objectives: ensure equitable access and uptake of HIV prevention programmes; scale up HIV testing; optimise rapid access to treatment and retention in care; improve quality of life for people living with HIV and address stigma; and stabilise and support system enablers, including the wider sexual and reproductive health system.

Obstructive Sleep Apnoea (OSA) is a prevalent sleep-related respiratory disorder characterised by recurrent upper airway obstruction during sleep, resulting in intermittent pauses in breathing. This leads to fragmented sleep, excessive daytime sleepiness, and significantly increases the risk of developing serious comorbidities such as hypertension, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and stroke. OSA affects approximately 5% of the population, with a substantial proportion remaining undiagnosed. The condition is particularly burdensome in individuals with coexisting chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) or obesity hypoventilation syndrome (OSAHS), where symptoms and health risks are further exacerbated.

Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) therapy is the first-line treatment for OSA, delivering a constant flow of air via a mask to maintain airway patency during sleep. Effective management requires consistent nightly use. CPAP devices typically have a lifespan of 7 years, while masks are single-patient use items requiring replacement every 6 to 12 months and regular patient cleaning to ensure optimal function and hygiene.

opportunities.name: Point-of-care (POC) blood gas analysers
opportunities.authority: Gloucestershire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
opportunities.description:
The blood gas service at Gloucestershire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (GHNHSFT) is integral to the delivery of point-of-care testing (POCT) diagnostics, supporting rapid clinical decision-making at or near the patient bedside. This service underpins multidisciplinary teams across a range of acute and specialist care environments within the Trust’s two main acute hospitals: Gloucestershire Royal Hospital (GRH) and Cheltenham General Hospital (CGH).

Currently, the blood gas service supports approximately 100,000 near-patient test episodes annually, with activity distributed across both hospital sites.

The core requirement is the supply and maintenance of point-of-care (POC) blood gas analysers and all associated consumables for use in clinical settings such as hospitals, intensive care units, and emergency departments. Emphasis is placed on robust, user-friendly devices that minimise manual intervention, have a compact footprint, and offer full connectivity with hospital IT systems.

opportunities.description:
The Department of Health and Social Care is conducting a research project to understand current commissioning practices in community health, with the aim to support best practice including on outcomes for patients and communities.



As part of this research, the Department invites those involved in contracting and commissioning community health services within ICBs, local authorities and Places to complete a survey on their experiences in commissioning community health services.


Background


The government is committed to transforming the national health system, with key priorities including shifting care from hospitals to homes and focusing on early detection and prevention. As part of this, there is also a focus on developing neighbourhood health services that delivers care closer to home, enhances access, and improves patient outcomes while ensuring the sustainability of integrated health and social care services.



Community Health Services will be central to these transformations, and smarter commissioning that follow patient needs and supports innovation as part of an integrated neighbourhood health service is paramount.

His Majesty’s Government (HMG) has identified the life sciences as one of eight crucial growth-driving sectors for the UK economy. The life sciences are undergoing a scientific and technological revolution, and the UK is well placed to lead this new era of biomedical science. To this end, HMG has been developing an ambitious and targeted sector plan for the life sciences to build on these strengths and improve healthcare in the UK.

To support HMG’s broad strategic goals for the life sciences, the Department of Health & Social Care (DHSC) is conducting this market engagement to better understand the capacity and technical capabilities of the UK biobanking market – covering both the storage and processing of biological samples (“bio-samples”).

The purpose of this engagement is to gather information on the UK biobanking market’s:
• current capacity for bio-sample storage and processing,
• technical capabilities for storage and processing,
• existing investment plans, and
• timescales for potential expansion.

opportunities.authority: Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC)
opportunities.description:
1.	Purpose
DHSC is conducting a market engagement exercise to understand more about the companies and services in the UK that can, or that are seeking to produce, distribute, supply and store different formulations of take-home naloxone that can reverse the effect of an opioid overdose. In particular, we are looking to understand how these suppliers and manufacturers could potentially meet the future of needs of a UK Buffer Stock of Naloxone. The outcome of the market engagement will inform decisions around potential future procurement and storage of a naloxone buffer stock as well as providing information on how the market could meet a potential increase in demand across the UK.

opportunities.name: DHSC: GPH: National Drug Treatment Monitoring System (NDTMS)
opportunities.authority: Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC)
opportunities.description: Our requirement is for a supplier to produce analysis and statistical information to support local commissioning of drug and alcohol treatment using data from NDTMS. This will include independent production of national and official statistics publications and supporting data, independent verification of responses to FOI and PQ requests, and research publications requiring academic expertise. We also require the supplier to produce and support the web presence of public access national statistics from data collected through the National Drug Treatment Monitoring System, and provide professional reporting of management information via restricted, secure access routes. Data from the National Drug Treatment Monitoring System (NDTMS) provides a key mechanism for monitoring the successful delivery of drug and alcohol treatment services. The government has stated several specific ambitions for expanding drug treatment capacity and improve the quality of provision, where performance is supported by timely and accessible monitoring of data from the NDTMS.

opportunities.authority: East of England Collaborative Procurement Hub
opportunities.description:
We want to hear from organisations that deliver services with a social impact - that is, services which create positive change for people and communities. These go beyond meeting immediate needs, focusing instead on improving lives, reducing inequalities, and strengthening communities. Examples include support for employment, mental health, homelessness prevention, or improving access to green spaces.
This pre-market engagement will help us understand the range of services currently available and shape a framework that is practical, accessible, and easy to use for both buyers and suppliers.
The East of England NHS Collaborative Procurement Hub (the Hub) is developing a clear and flexible route for public sector bodies, including the NHS, to commission high-quality services that address the wider determinants of health – such as education, employment, and community safety.
This market engagement will help us to:
•	Understand the services you offer.
•	Identify barriers that may prevent you from using the framework.
•	Ensure the framework is suitable for organisations of all sizes.
•	Strike the right balance between national consistency and local flexibility.

opportunities.authority: Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC)
opportunities.description:
Expression of Interest Deadline: 19/03/2025 
Engagement Event Date(s): 20/03/2025 


Background
The government has committed to end new HIV transmissions in England by 2030 and is developing a new HIV Action Plan (HIVAP) which will be published this year.


Collaboration is at the core of the new HIVAP and the government is engaging with a wide range of system partners in its development, including people with lived experience, the voluntary and community sector, professional bodies, primary care, and local partners amongst others.  


The new HIVAP will have 5 key objectives: ensure equitable access and uptake of HIV prevention programmes; scale up HIV testing; optimise rapid access to treatment and retention in care; improve quality of life for people living with HIV and address stigma; and stabilise and support system enablers, including the wider sexual and reproductive health system.  


Objective
We are trying to understand the steps that are needed to ensure that we meet the 2030 target of no new HIV transmissions within England and prioritise the necessary actions.  


The objective of this roundtable is to gain insights on the challenges that we may face

For this reason, an Independent Mental Health Act Advocate (IMHA) service is provided to patients of the ELFT Forensic Service by The Advocacy Project, which is commissioned by London Borough of Hackney. If a service user has been assessed as having a lack of mental capacity in relation to making a specific decision about their lives, a best interests decision is made under the Mental Capacity Act and this is supported by an Independent Mental Capacity Advocate, as required within the Mental Capacity Act (2015), which is also provided by The Advocacy Project. Finally, Care Act Advocacy is provided by The Advocacy Project in relation to the Care Act (2014).

opportunities.description:
Tenders are invited from establishments who have the capabilities to take on all services related to transgenic colony management. 

At the MHRA, the Biological Services facility houses two transgenic mouse breeding colonies. These colonies have been specifically bred to support the Poliomyelitis test work implemented by the Science, Research & Innovation Group. 

In-bred transgenic mice with the Human Polio receptor gene provides a practical alternative to the use of non-human primates. These lines are used to assess the neurovirulence of polioviruses and immunogenicity/ protection of vaccines and hence play a key role in the global polio activities of the agency. Both colonies require refresh, as genetic drift has been observed due to multiple unexpected phenotypic changes. We are therefore seeking assistance in the maintenance and refresh of colonies, possibly looking to utilise already frozen stocks of embryos/ sperm.

opportunities.name: Smart Predictive Building Maintenance, Green Spaces and Associated Services DPS
opportunities.authority: Countess of Chester Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
opportunities.description:
This DPS provides the public sector with a means to leverage Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, data analytics, and machine learning to monitor the health and conditions of buildings, as well as significantly enhance the management and experience of green spaces.

By collecting and analysing data on performance, environmental conditions, and usage patterns, solutions will predict potential failures and schedule maintenance proactively. Suppliers appointed to this DPS will harness and deliver Smart Predictive Building Maintenance, Green Spaces and Associated Services solutions. Solutions may include a range of sensors from a range of protocols to collect data on, but are not limited to:
• Air quality
• Presence
• Noise
• Light
• Moisture
• Water temperature and flow
• Fill Level (Capacity)
• Load
• Corrosion
• Gas and Electricity Consumption

Data collected from IoT sensors across buildings and green spaces provides valuable insights that can inform long-term strategic planning. Public Sector Organisations can use this data to forecast future maintenance needs, budget more effectively, and plan sustainable development projects that align with environmental targets.

opportunities.name: PRJ 1388 Parents in Mind (Newham)
opportunities.authority: NHS North East London Integrated Care Board
opportunities.description:
NHS North East London ICB is seeking to commission a perinatal peer support service for mothers and birthing parents (MBP) and fathers and non-birthing parents (FNBP) in Newham who struggle with perinatal mental illness. The service will support parents during pregnancy and up to two years post birth. It will have a pathway for mothers and birthing parents, as well as a pathway for fathers and non-birthing parents. Parents will have the opportunity to engage with support groups and therapeutic activities, as well as 1:1 peer support. The service will aim to match parents with peer supporters who have similar lived experiences. Support should be provided in-person at accessible venues throughout Newham (e.g. children’s centres), and the provider should offer online/telephone appointments too.

The service will have a target of providing support to 150 parents (at least 70 of which should be fathers or non-birthing parents). Parents supported 1:1 and attendees at in-person group events will count towards this target.

opportunities.name: Nurse Call System Maintenance
opportunities.authority: Nottingham University Hospital NHS Trust
opportunities.description:
The Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust (The Trust) is conducting this request for information (RFI) exercise regarding the provision of a contract for both planned testing servicing and maintenance, as well as any reactive servicing, of the nurse call systems. The purpose of the contract is to enable the Trust to meet its needs as a provider of healthcare services. For example, enabling ward staff to respond quickly in event of a signal from patients for support or assistance.

The primary remit of NHS organisations with regard to nurse call systems is the safety of patients. For all premises under its control, it is therefore critical that the Trust’s nurse call systems are effectively serviced and maintained. Whilst it is not a legal requirement to service nurse call systems, it is understood they must be regularly maintained to ensure continued functionality.

Without regular maintenance, the system can fail when needed, risking patients’ lives. In addition, lack of maintenance can result in false alarms, leading to staff becoming desensitised to the system and the associated risk they may ignore it when a real emergency occurs.

opportunities.name: PRJ2126 SEL ICB School engagement to support Black and mixed Heritage Children
opportunities.authority: NHS South East London Integrated Care Board
opportunities.description:
NHS SEL ICB, hereafter referred to as 'Authority' wishes to commission and identify voluntary sector organisations to engage in this large-scale school engagement initiative. Addressing inequalities in mental healthcare for children and young people across South East London is a priority area of focus for the ICB – to this end, the ICB is partnering with Black Thrive to address mental health inequalities for Black and mixed heritage school aged children, and looking for addition local voluntary sector organisations to engage in community engagement. 
Based on review of stakeholder feedback and data, the ICB recommended that there is a need to develop and enhance access to trauma-informed, early intervention and prevention wellbeing and mental health support for Black and mixed heritage children. This Pilot Prototype is necessary to input into the Strategic Outline Business Cases (SOC) for the RAAC hospitals for the verification of corridor widths, which is fundamental to sizing of hospital size requirements (footprint) and H2.0 design. The majority of these SOC approval dates for the RAAC hospital are due Dec 24 / Jan 25.

opportunities.name: Archetype Decarbonisation Model & Guidance
opportunities.authority: NHS England
opportunities.description:
This project will capitalise on the success of creating a digital twin at an NHS trust. It will utilise digital twin technology to create a set of archetypes based on ERIC and other contextual data. A set of possible decarbonisation measures will be simulated to help identify technologies and interventions that will deliver carbon reduction to meet national targets. 
Understanding the order, cost and impact of low carbon technologies will allow heat and site decarbonisation plans to be aligned and templates to be developed, thereby reducing the costs for planning and ensuring that organisations without energy management resources can develop a plan for investment.

The Psychological Wellbeing Service will complement the wider offer for early intervention, to facilitate choice and increase capacity.   The service will be provided to children and young people aged from 10-18 years old and for parenting interventions from 5 years upwards.

By expanding the existing early intervention offer and integrating this sub-contracting arrangement into the wider early intervention system in Hull and East Riding, we aim to stem the flow of referrals into core CAMHS. This will reduce the existing waiting list, alongside ensuring C&YP and their families receive timely support and intervention around their needs as they arise, reducing long waits and potential exacerbation of needs. New referrals deemed appropriate for low intensity interventions will be seen by the service. It is our intention that this will facilitate a quicker response for children and young people with mild to moderate mental health needs and free up capacity within the CAMHS service to respond to an ongoing increase in urgent complex referrals which is having an impact on waiting times.

opportunities.name: Evaluation of a sample of Public Sector Decarbonisation Scheme funded projects
opportunities.authority: NHS England
opportunities.description:
The Public Sector Decarbonisation Scheme, managed by DESNZ, has provided over £1BN of funds to NHS trusts to deliver carbon reduction programmes since 2020/21.  Many of these projects have already been delivered, some of which are examplar in nature for the NHS estate.  Initial empirical data indicates a varied level of project carbon actual savings vs projected savings. This project would evaluate the outcomes of a cross sample of these decarbonisation projects across the NHS estate in England.  
Evaluating the impact of the installed technologies will allow further heat and site decarbonisation plans to be aligned, templates  developed and guidance created to support benefits realisation for projects, thereby reducing the costs for planning and ensuring that organisations without energy management resources can develop a plan for investment. This will ensure that the NHS can continue to deliver value for money across decarbonisation projects.

opportunities.name: Low carbon heat opportunity map
opportunities.authority: NHS England
opportunities.description:
This project would create an opportunity map which consolidates the myriad of low carbon heating options available to decarbonise the NHS estate. It will consolidate information available on heat network sources (planned and existing) and emerging sources of low carbon fuels, such as hydrogen or biogas. This map will ensure that trusts and NHS buildings that are in areas of planned or existing heat networks, planned hydrogen or biogas sources, would be informed of these systems. It will provide / complete an initial desktop assessment to help appraise these opportunities in lieu of alternative electric-led heat sources. This enables the NHS estate to move to low carbon heat sources in the most economically advantageous way and allows the NHS to deliver its role as an anchor institute. 
The deliverable of this project will be a guidance document which gives financial, carbon and planning advice to NHS organisations that might benefit from low carbon heat sources. This document will enable trusts to understand the opportunities from low carbon heat and support their business cases for heat decarbonisation. opportunities.name: FIT@80 Evaluation
opportunities.authority: NHS England
opportunities.description:
To support achievement of NHS Long Term Plan ambitions, it has been agreed by NHS England that the NHS Bowel Cancer Screening Programme referral threshold will reduce from 120 ug/gm to 80ug/gm, in line with the Scottish screening programme. Evidence suggests that this will be a cost-effective way to detect more cancers earlier, reduce mortality and increase quality of life. 

Achieving this extension will be challenging alongside year-on-year increases in endoscopy demand from symptomatic services, BSCP age extension, and the enrolment of people with Lynch syndrome into the programme. Therefore, to understand how this change in screening protocol can be delivered sustainably it has been agreed that the threshold will initially be dropped in select pilot sites alongside a comprehensive evaluation.

This business case seeks approval to procure a partner to deliver the evaluation.

opportunities.name: PRJ1377 SEL ICB Population Health Management
opportunities.authority: NHS South East London Integrated Care Board
opportunities.description:
This specification outlines the requirements for a Population Health Management (PHM) tool to be used within Lambeth Health and Care Partnership. The tool will extract data from primary care systems, aggregate and present this data on dashboards for various healthcare areas , and provide functionalities to enable GPs to re-identify patients for actionable interventions.
Objectives
The PHM tool aims to:
• Aggregate data from primary care systems.
• Present data on user-friendly dashboards for healthcare areas such as flu vaccination, NHS health checks, blood pressure, and diabetes.
• Allow GPs to re-identify patients for intervention purposes.
• Display near real-time data.
• Explain business rules and criteria clearly on the dashboards.
• Offer ongoing training and support.
• Provide functionality to link additional datasets in the future.
• Support different levels of user access based on permissions.
• Show baseline metrics, trends over time, and outcomes.
• Enable segmentation to identify patient cohorts for targeted interventions.

For clarification questions please see attached the clarification template and use to submit any questions.

opportunities.authority: Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC)
opportunities.description: The Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) has spoken to a wide range of Local Authorities (LAs) and IT suppliers about the challenges and opportunities they face in the Adult Social Care sector. A consistent theme came up – that the Case Management System (CMS) market was not functioning effectively; systems were not performing as expected, LAs were finding procurement excessively difficult, and suppliers were facing major cost pressures. DHSC decided to explore this market in more detail and provide greater support. This is to enable the market to sustainably innovate and produce efficient and effective systems that best serve the needs of people requiring care.

opportunities.name: Impact Evaluation of Virtual Wards
opportunities.authority: NHS England
opportunities.description:
The purpose of this contract is to evaluate the impact and effectiveness of virtual wards as an intervention to better manage demand and capacity in secondary care, whilst supporting optimal patient outcomes.  The evaluation will set out to understand the following: 

1. Effectiveness of reducing the number of avoidable hospital admissions 
2. The impact on hospital demand and capacity 
3. Understand the relative equivalence of a virtual ward admission avoidance activity compared with an emergency medical admission in an acute hospital setting. 
4. The cost-effectiveness of VWs to the health system and wider social care system.
5. Assessment of health inequalities, including access and outcomes
6. A recommended methodological approach to ongoing evaluations, which can be developed into a toolkit.
7. Enablers and blockers to uptake and impact of VW in secondary care and social care
8. Impact VWs on patient outcomes.

opportunities.name: Physical Restraint In Mental Health Inpatient Settings Training
opportunities.authority: NHS England
opportunities.description:
The Reducing Restrictive Practices Oversight Group (RPOG) has proposed a review of the different types of restraint training that are offered across NHS services.
Whilst the overall aim of any work in this space is to promote least restrictive options and avoid restraint wherever possible, it is recognised that in some circumstances, physical intervention may be required to protect people’s right to life.                     
We propose to undertake a scoping review of all of the physical restraint training systems implemented within NHS Commissioned Mental health inpatient services across England., to review any common themes, gaps and risks and review instances of specialist adaptations for specific needs such as restraint in children and young people and for those with an eating disorder or additional physical health need. To share findings and recommendations as a result of the review, giving particular consideration to whether a standardised approach to restraint training within the NHS and across NHS commissioned MH inpatient services would be of benefit to staff, patients and organisations.

opportunities.name: Benefits support for Population Health & Care Programme
opportunities.authority: Lewisham and Greenwich NHS Trust
opportunities.description:
The population health Programme uses the Oracle Population Health platform (HealtheIntent) which has been in place since 2020.

HealtheIntent provides is an integrated data set comprising of four core data sources that refresh overnight to give almost real time patient identifiable data.  There is also the ability to use the platform to upload other data sources as a snapshot in a semi-automated way as has been the case for the patient tracking list for surgery and adult social care data.

The contract for HealtheIntent is up for review in March 2025 when it has one more year to run until March 2026.  A decision will need to be made as to whether the contract is extended beyond March 2026 for a further year or if there is likely viable alternative to switch over from HealtheIntent to a London platform - assuming such an alternative is ready to use from March 2026.

We are looking to have a final report ready for review by the Population Health and Care Board and other SE London stakeholders by March to inform the contract decision from April 2025.

The total estimated lifetime value of the contract is £7,127,600 for the 3 year contract plus the optional extension period of 2 years; this is split to £1,781,900 for Lot 1 (Herefordshire), and £5,345,700 for Lot 2 (Worcestershire). opportunities.authority: Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
opportunities.description: IMPEDE-PKD is a global clinical trial, with a recruitment target of over 1000 participants (with 300 being recruited in the UK). It is a pragmatic, multi-centre, double blind parallel group randomised controlled trial of metformin versus placebo in patients with Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD). The primary objective is to evaluate the long-term efficacy of metformin therapy in slowing the rate of kidney function decline in metformin versus placebo treated ADPKD subjects. In the UK, the trial will also be using the UK validated and standardised ADPKD-Pain Assessment Tool (APAT) to measure and evaluate the characteristics of pain. ADPKD is a leading cause of kidney failure and accounts for 11% of prevalent UK kidney replacement therapy (KRT) patients. Rapidly expanding cysts damage the kidney parenchyma causing kidney failure, debilitating chronic pain and reduced quality of life. Currently tolvaptan is the only licensed treatment. opportunities.name: Targeted Lung Health Check Outsourced Services (THLC)
opportunities.authority: Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust
opportunities.description:
The Targeted Lung Health Check service is divided into three service components:

•	Service Component 1 - Conducting Lung Health Checks, communicating results, managing all patient reminders for the incident round, and scheduling follow-up appointments.

•	Service Component 2 - Managing scanner schedules, including radiographers, assistants, nurses, and HCAs for the unit. This also includes IMER checks, CT scans, PACS storage, and sharing data with all providers.

•	Service Component 3 - Handling all CT radiology reporting, transferring CT reports to all providers, and managing PACS storage. Focusing on ongoing quality and service improvement, particularly in quality assurance and data management, with a commitment to monitoring and reporting an exemplary service with continuous development.

Potential bidders are being invited to tender for the full service and/ or one or both service components 1 and 3, allowing the Trust to determine the package that will deliver the best value for money.

opportunities.name: NRL for chemical hazards
opportunities.authority: Food Standards Agency
opportunities.description:
The FSA and FSS are responsible for Official Feed and Food Controls across the UK. The UK has a legal obligation to appoint NRLs for feed and food. NRLs provide advice and support to food, feed, and food contact materials enforcement laboratories and the FSA and FSS to ensure a harmonised approach to food safety enforcement. NRLs are responsible for setting standards for routine procedures and reliable testing methods in the regulated areas of feed and food. This delivers consumer protection and effective, risk-based, and proportionate regulation and enforcement.  

The appointed laboratory will carry out the provision of services for the UK National Reference Laboratory (NRL) for Chemical Hazards in feed and food. Chemical hazards in feed and food could include, but are not limited to:  
- Food Contact Materials (FCM),  
- Processing contaminants, 
- Mycotoxins and plant toxins,  
- Metals and nitrogenous compounds,  
- Halogenated persistent organic pollutants,  
-Flavourings.

There are two main commissioning bodies that use a prior approval system within NHS England: The Managed Access Funds (Cancer Drugs Fund and Innovative Medicines Fund) and Routine Commissioning.
Amongst the features of the operating model for the commissioning bodies is a single web-based registration system and an IT infrastructure which supports web-based access for all clinicians across the country. We are looking to undertake a discovery phase to understand which Suppliers can host the system with finances available.
