opportunities.name: DHSC:RFI Employers’ Services Organisation Contract for the NHS in England.
opportunities.authority: Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC)
opportunities.description:
To support workforce policy development within DHSC by feeding in a unified employer voice from across the whole NHS in England, 
The Contract will consist of 9 work programmes covering workforce policy which will be agreed on an annual basis. The proposed work programmes are as follows:   
Work Programme 1: Pay and Contracts 
Work Programme 2: Education, skills, and redesign of workforce  
Work Programme 3: International Recruitment  
Work Programme 4: Workforce Supply and Retention  
Work Programme 5: Pensions and total reward   
Work Programme 6: Employment services   
Work Programme 7: Staff Experience   
Work Programme 8: Staff Engagement including Social Partnership Forum (SPF)   
Work Programme 9: Communications  
The aims of this contract are to:   
Support the NHS with the development, implementation and delivery of workforce policies  
Build and maintain networks with NHS senior workforce leaders  
Execute the deliverables detailed in Work Programmes 1-9 inclusive on an annual basis  
Respond and action any ad hoc requirements of DHSC i.e., any changes in legislation or to reflect any changes in ministerial/DHSC priority over the course of the year.

opportunities.name: NW2024-61 Adult ADHD Accreditation Framework
opportunities.authority: NHS Norfolk and Waveney Integrated Care Board
opportunities.description:
Norfolk and Waveney Integrated Board  and Cambridge and Peterborough Integrated Care Board  both have Adult ADHD Assessment and Treatment services commissioned offer through  from local Mental Health Trusts. These are successful small teams. However, with the advent of COVID-19, partnered with an exponential increase in referrals both ICBs need to commission additional services under a Framework to assist with the current wait list and to offer patient choice in line with national guidance / policy. 
Alongside this, further work is happening to look at how we can re-design the service to meet increased demands. This includes a redesign of the ADHD pathway in both systems. Providers delivering services to both ICBs can therefore expect changes, during the life of the contract, in the local treatment and intervention offers and referral, triage, and screening arrangements, that they need to adapt and respond to.

There are no finances attached to this Framework as providers will invoice the ICB(s) under the current Right to Choose process – this will be detailed for those providers that join the Framework.

opportunities.name: DHSC: Nursing and Nursing Associates Engagement
opportunities.authority: Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC)
opportunities.description:
In December 2021, the government published ‘People at the Heart of Care: Adult Social Care Reform White Paper’ which outlined a 10-year vision including reforms for how we will transform support and care in England, and work “to build a workforce of the right size with the right skills to meet the growing need for care and support”. In April 2023, the government published ‘Next steps to put People at the Heart of Care’, outlining a clear plan on how to achieve this. In 2024 the government announced the latest tranche of workforce reforms including the launch of the first ever national career structure for the care workforce, alongside a new nationally accredited social care qualification, and social work and social care nursing apprenticeships.  

The Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) are seeking to secure a supplier to deliver support to aid the recruitment and retention of nurses and nursing associates in the Adult Social Care (ASC) workforce that will form an integral part of the new core adult social care workforce support and improvement offer and will compliment the nursing apprenticeship fund.

opportunities.description:
Throughout 2022 and 2023, the Genomics Unit has been running a requirements phase for a national Genomics Ordering Management Project.  The Genomics Ordering management project is designed to streamline and optimise the genomics test order management between primary, secondary, and tertiary care settings (within England) and the NHS Genomic Medicine Service for WGS (Whole Genome Sequencing) and Non-WGS (Non-Whole Genome Sequencing) genomics testing pathways. In this context, interoperability is defined as the ability to electronically request, process, manage and track genomic requests, samples, results and reports across multiple settings in a standardised approach. 

Key deliverables from this phase include:

• EHR(s)
• LIMS(s)
• A web portal
• NGIS infrastructure

opportunities.name: Children’s Cancer Network PTC - Media and Stakeholder Engagement (Post Decision)
opportunities.authority: NHS England
opportunities.description:
NHS England have recently taken a decision on the future location of specialised children’s cancer services here; work now commences to implement the service change.   
The programme remains high-profile and we must continue to engage with a wide range of stakeholders.  This includes being 'on the front foot' with regards media and public affairs who will continue to be important stakeholders.   The skills to do this are a material gap within the Programme.  There is not enough capacity or relevant expertise within the current NHSE comms team or with any other teams that we are working with.  Now that a decision has been made; it will be important that we can get the next phase of the programme underway as smoothly as possible.  
Failure to resource the media, communications, public affairs  and parliamentary side of this work is a serious reputational and programme risk.  Maintenance of relationships with local politicians, MPs and with the media will continue to be important.   
External support is therefore required.

opportunities.name: Impact and economic evaluation of Virtual Wards
opportunities.authority: NHS England
opportunities.description:
Our aim is to determine the impact and effectiveness of virtual wards as an intervention to better manage demand and capacity in secondary care, whilst supporting optimal patient outcomes.
There is an urgent need to evaluate virtual wards to determine:
1. The effectiveness of VWs in reducing the number of avoidable hospital admissions (Step-up )
2. The impact of VWs on hospital demand and capacity (Step-up & Step-down)
3. While there is a debate about the bed-based approach to quantifying capacity in VWs, there is a need to understand the relative equivalence of a virtual ward admission avoidance activity compared with an emergency medical admission in an acute hospital setting. There are several important factors to consider, such as the number of virtual ward admissions that end in a hospital admission and the case mix of patients including how unwell they are.
4. The cost-effectiveness of VWs to the health system and wider social care system.
5. Assessment of health inequalities, including access and outcomes

A standard pulmonary rehabilitation programme should consist of a minimum of 6 weeks of two sessions per week physical exercise, disease education, nutritional, psychological, and behavioural interventions. opportunities.description:
During the Covid-19 pandemic a staff support hub was set up in Norfolk & Waveney as part of a national initiative to provide additional mental health support to health & social care staff who were struggling with the impact of Covid. National funding for these hubs ceased in March 2023, with each ICS required to provide health & social care staff a similar level of support to the Covid hubs on an on-going basis. 
Following a review of existing service provision, commissioners have identified the need to develop tier 3.5 - 4 enhanced psychological services (EPS) to complement existing tier 1-3 provision. The service is targeted at staff with more complex clinical presentations that typically require a higher degree of face-to-face interventions. The tier 3.5 - 4 enhanced psychological services will primarily support individual staff with their mental health but will also occasionally be offered to their wider teams.

opportunities.name: Therapeutic Apheresis Services (TAS) - Digitally Managed Service (DMS) - RFI
opportunities.authority: NHS Blood and Transplant
opportunities.description:
This is a Request for Information (RFI) only and will be used to gather market information and engage with suppliers who may be able to support NHSBT to digitise this service.

Apheresis is a process in which a particular substance or part of someone's blood is removed from the blood and the rest returned to their body. NHSBT’s Therapeutic Apheresis Services (TAS) was developed from a medical and nursing interest in collection and therapeutic apheresis and became an independent function in 2008/9.  The aim was to become the pre-ferred provider of high quality, cost-effective therapeutic apheresis services and reduce in-equities of access to treatment across the UK. 

The service is part of NHSBT’s Cell, Apheresis and Gene Therapies Function treating adults and children, providing TAS across England to around 1600 adult and paediatric patients each year.  The service is based within 8 units across the UK, but also cover >45 acute trusts as an outreach service, including access to a 24/7 emergency apheresis service.

opportunities.name: East of England Cancer Alliance (South) NHS-Galleri Interim Implementation Pilot
opportunities.authority: NHS England
opportunities.description:
The Provision of a high quality clinical service based in the community to support the East of England Cancer Alliance (South) to deliver the NHS-Galleri Interim Implementation Pilot.

The NHS-Galleri blood test enables early Cancer Detection.

NHS England has agreed to purchase 1 million Galleri tests over 2 years that will be offered to asymptomatic participants aged 50-77 years old in Cancer Alliances not involved in the initial NHS Galleri Clinical Trial. Given the East of England Cancer Alliance (South) was not involved in the initial clinical trial, they have been selected to participate in the NHS-Galleri Interim Implementation Pilot by the National Cancer Programme Team. The pilot will cover all Integrated Care Boards within the East of England Cancer Alliance (South) region, which includes Hertfordshire and West Essex, Mid and South Essex and Bedford, Luton and Milton Keynes ICBs.

*Please note this opportunity is only open to bidders on RM6100 who responded positively to the RFI*

NHSBT provides a blood and transplant service to the NHS. Every year, our volunteer donors give around 2 million blood donations and 3,500 organs – saving and transforming countless lives.
We currently have circa 52 mobile Blood Donation teams, who collect around 75% of our whole blood donations within local communities. This involves travelling to locations, such as Town Halls and Community Centres, setting up a Blood Donation Session for the day, taking donations from local blood donors and then packing up the session, and repeating this at a different location on the next working day. 
In addition to this, we also have circa 25 Blood Donor Centres, which collect around 25% of our whole blood donations and other blood components. These centres are generally situated within cities, towns and hospital bases. We are looking to expand this capability by opening a donor centre every year and we would need to have a Supplier to support any expansion.

Throughout 2022 and 2023, the Genomics Unit has been running a requirements phase for a national Genomics Ordering Management Project. opportunities.name: Developing a national resolution policy and framework for improvement management
opportunities.authority: NHS England
opportunities.description:
The development of a standard set of simplified national people policies by 2025 is a key action within the Future of NHS HR and OD report (FHROD).  

Currently, each NHS organisation creates its own policies and framework for resolution, which can lead to considerable management capacity being allocated to policy development and variation in the approach taken to resolution of workplace conflicts.  A simplified and standardised approach to workplace resolution is intended to embed a just culture approach within the NHS, incorporating in one framework disciplinary, capability, grievance, and bullying/harassment policies.

The national resolution policy and framework for the NHS will help NHS organisations to:

a)	realign behaviours, build relationships, and create long-term solutions to workplace conflicts and complaints.

b)	disseminate the people-centred and values-based cultural benefits from the resolution policy and framework across the NHS.

c)	reduce the stress, the cost and the distress that is commonly caused by formal grievance procedures.

Pulmonary rehabilitation is a multidisciplinary, individually- tailored programme that promotes self-care and self-management for patients with chronic respiratory impairment. To achieve maximum health gains, comprehensive programmes need to include the following fundamental components: disease education, self-management advice and structured physical exercise. 
A standard pulmonary rehabilitation programme should consist of a minimum of 6 weeks of two sessions per week physical exercise, disease education, nutritional, psychological, and behavioural interventions. The service will assess, counsel, enable and support patients through the programme and carry out appropriate tests to measure efficacy of outcome. The service will plan and administer booking arrangements for patients.

the most deprived 20% of the national population PLUS:

opportunities.name: Northwick Park Hospital Discharge Support Service
opportunities.authority: NHS North West London Integrated Care Board
opportunities.description:
NHS North West London requires the provision of Northwick Park Hospital Discharge Support Service for Harrow and Brent residents starting from the 1st of June 2024 for 3yrs. 

The service helps vulnerable people in Northwick Park Hospital (Harrow and Brent residents) to be safely discharged home where social factors are impacting and delaying discharge from hospital.
Key requirements include:
•	Streamlines the discharge, supporting Pathways P0 and P1, by getting patients home as quickly as possible.
•	Ensures vulnerable older people settle at home and maximise their independence.
•	Empowers individuals to maximise choice and control over their life and promote healt h and well-being.
•	Enables people to continue to live in their own home for longer and to avoid or delay the need for costly support services and packages of care later.

opportunities.description:
NICE is holding a virtual supplier event about its Access and Identity Management System (AIMS) on April 16th 2026, 11:30am to 1pm as part of procurement activities for a new 3-year contract (plus 2 x 12-month).

This system provides secure authentication and authorisation for eligible NHS and wider health and social care staff seeking who want to digital knowledge resources purchased by national, regional and local health organisations.

AIMS comprises two interdependent components delivered as a single, integrated service:

(1) an Identity Provider (IdP) service, which isan “identify management” capability to manage user identification and authentication; and

(2) a Federated Access Management service, which is a “publisher federation” capability to manage integration with publisher platforms and ensures users receive the correct access rights. Maintaining this integration is essential to guarantee continuity of access to evidence for the healthcare workforce and to uphold contractual obligations with publishers.

opportunities.name: Wheelchairs and Specialist Seating Services
opportunities.authority: NHS Sussex Integrated Care Board
opportunities.description:
NHS Sussex Integrated Care Board (ICB) is looking to provide a contract to provide wheelchair and specialist seating services to the population of Sussex for a 5 + 2 year contract, commencing 1st April 2027.
The Sussex Wheelchair Service provides a comprehensive, integrated service for adults, children, and young people with long-term mobility needs. 
Service users have described a wheelchair as a vehicle of freedom
opportunities.category:
highlighting both the emotional and functional significance of the service.
 The service supports individuals to optimise their independence, health outcomes, and quality of life through timely access to assessment, provision, maintenance, and review of appropriate wheeled mobility equipment. The service is designed to be equitable, needs-led, and responsive, ensuring consistent and high-quality provision across Sussex. It includes both manual and powered wheelchairs, pressure-relieving cushions, and postural management equipment, tailored to meet long-term clinical needs.
The Specialist Postural Static Seating Service will be for adults in East Sussex.
Annual contract value: £8,436,258
Estimated total contract value including 2 year extension: £59,053,806 (5 year contract + 2 year extension)
Proposed contract start date: 1st April, 2027.

opportunities.name: Havering - Crisis Cafe
opportunities.authority: North East London NHS Foundation Trust
opportunities.description:
Havering specialist mental health crisis pathway is made up of inpatient beds, psychiatric liaison, crisis resolution and home treatment teams, clinical decision unit, and a 24-hour Mental Health Direct Line. 
These services are delivering largely positive outcomes for users, carers and families. There is significant capacity issues and rising demand impacting on the services’ ability to respond in a timely way based on recent ED attendance data  
This delay to access is placing increasing pressure on the emergency services, such as ED, LAS, and Police, as people experiencing mental health crisis seek quicker access to support elsewhere. 
The model set out in this specification will deliver better patient outcomes by offering an additional option in the local system for crisis support that is accessible out of hours and provides an alternative to NHS emergency care  provision in Havering. This option will be a non-clinical offering a therapeutic and social support in an approach that ensure care is delivered with a patient centred engaged way.
